Temporarily extracts and returns a terminator only when the target block is empty and consists solely of a `Goto`; otherwise returns `None`, including loop-entry cases where the terminator is already absent. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Collapses a chain of empty goto-only blocks so a successor points directly at the final destination, while restoring intermediate terminators and updating predecessor counts consistently. This method calls `impl<'a, 'tcx> CfgSimplifier<'a, 'tcx>::take_terminator_if_simple_goto` repeatedly to walk the chain.

If the current terminator is a `Goto` to a block with exactly one predecessor, replaces the current terminator with the successor’s terminator, records that successor for later statement splicing, and marks the merged block dead. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Rewrites a `SwitchInt` terminator into a `Goto` when all switch edges target the same block, adjusting predecessor counts to remove the redundant incoming edges. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Removes all `StatementKind::Nop` statements from every basic block before CFG restructuring begins. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Simplifies a `SwitchInt` terminator by removing explicit switch arms whose target is identical to the `otherwise` target, then rebuilding the switch target table. It does not call other listed methods.

Finds unreachable empty non-cleanup blocks, and when more than one exists, rewrites all references to duplicate blocks to a single representative by visiting the body. This method explicitly calls `simplify_duplicate_switch_targets` indirectly through the visitor used during `visit_body`.
Returns the visitor's stored `TyCtxt`. It does not call other listed methods.

Rewrites terminator successor edges that point to duplicate unreachable blocks so they all target the canonical block, then normalizes any affected `SwitchInt` terminator. This method explicitly calls `simplify_duplicate_switch_targets`.

Deletes unreachable basic blocks by computing reachability, compacting live blocks to the front, optionally preserving coverage metadata with `save_unreachable_coverage`, truncating dead tails, and remapping all terminator successors to the new block indices.

Preserves coverage information across dead-block removal by identifying inlined instances that still have live counters, nopping obsolete live-block coverage statements, collecting unreachable coverage regions for still-live instances, and re-emitting them as `Unreachable` coverage statements in the start block. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the pass-specific static name string for the current `SimplifyLocals` variant. It does not call other listed methods.
Enables the `SimplifyLocals` pass only when MIR optimization level is greater than zero. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Entry point for the local-simplification MIR pass; logs execution and delegates to `simplify_locals`.

Iteratively removes storage statements and definitions whose destination locals are no longer used, repeating until no more statements can be deleted. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::is_used` to test liveness and `impl UsedLocals::statement_removed` to decrement counts for each removed statement.

Shrinks the local-declaration set by first building use counts with `impl UsedLocals::new`, then iteratively deleting removable unused definitions with `remove_unused_definitions`, constructing a remapping with `make_local_map`, and finally rewriting local references if any locals were removed.

Builds the old-to-new local remapping by compacting all used locals to the front of `local_decls`, swapping declarations into place and truncating unused trailing entries. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::is_used` to decide which locals are retained.
Creates a `UsedLocals` analyzer with zeroed use counts, records the argument boundary, and populates counts by visiting the whole MIR body. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Reports whether a local must be retained, treating the return place and arguments as always used and otherwise checking for a nonzero recorded use count. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Updates use counts after a statement deletion by switching the visitor into decrement mode and revisiting the removed statement through `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for UsedLocals::visit_statement`.

Processes the left-hand side of an assignment-like statement: indirect places are treated as ordinary uses, while direct definitions skip counting the base local and only visit projection operands. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Custom statement visitor for local-use analysis: it ignores nops and storage annotations, fully visits side-effecting statements, and for removable assignments or deinitialization-like statements counts only the relevant uses/definitions. This method calls `impl UsedLocals::visit_lhs` for assignment/deinitialization targets.
Adjusts a local’s use count during traversal, incrementing during normal analysis and decrementing when replaying a removed statement. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Iteratively removes unused storage, assignment, discriminant, deinit, and nop statements until local-usage updates reach a fixed point, keeping MIR CFG structure intact. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the local-remapping visitor. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Rewrites each visited local in place according to the compacting map, assuming the local was retained. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/dest_pr: Checks whether the destination-propagation MIR pass should run by querying the session MIR optimization level via `mir_opt_level` and enabling the pass only at level 3 or higher.

Drives destination propagation to a fixed point. It gathers borrowed locals with `borrowed_locals`, discovers merge opportunities with `find_candidates`, computes liveness through `into_engine`, `iterate_to_fixpoint`, and `into_results_cursor`, emits diagnostics with `dest_prop_mir_dump`, filters unsafe candidates with `FilterInformation::filter_liveness`, selects a non-conflicting subset of merges, applies them with `apply_merges`, and finally cleans CFG leftovers with `remove_dead_blocks`.
Applies the selected local merges to the MIR by constructing a `Merger` visitor and invoking `visit_body_preserves_cfg` to rewrite locals without changing control flow.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the merger visitor; it does not call other methods from the list.
Rewrites a visited local if it appears in the merge map by looking it up with `get`; otherwise leaves it unchanged.

Rewrites statements during merge application. It removes `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` for merged locals using `contains` and `make_nop`, then delegates recursive rewriting with `super_statement`, and finally deletes copy/move assignments that became self-assignments by calling `make_nop`.
Filters a candidate destination vector in place by applying the provided predicate through `retain`, keeping only locals classified as `Keep`.
Filters the candidate list stored in one occupied map entry by calling `vec_filter_candidates`, and removes the whole entry with `remove` if the filtered list becomes empty.

Removes conflicting candidate pairs involving a local in both forward and reverse candidate maps. It calls `entry_filter_candidates` to prune forward entries and uses `retain` over the reverse map to synchronize removals back into the forward map.
Creates a temporary `FilterInformation` context and starts liveness-based candidate rejection by calling `internal_filter_liveness`.

Traverses the body in preorder and scans each block backward to compute conflicts at every program point. For each terminator it calls `seek_after_primary_effect`, `for_terminator`, and `apply_conflicts`; for each statement it calls `seek_after_primary_effect`, `for_statement`, and `apply_conflicts`.

Eliminates candidate merges that are invalid at the current location based on recorded writes and liveness. It calls `filter_candidates_by` and rejects pairs when the other local is live via `contains` or also written in the same step, except for the special skipped assignment-use pair.

Collects write/read information for a statement after first clearing prior state with `reset`. For assignments it records the destination with `add_place`, records operand effects with `add_operand`, and for simple `Use` assignments also calls `consider_skipping_for_assign_use`; for discriminant/deinit/retag writes it records the written place with `add_place`.

Recognizes an assignment-use pair that should be exempted from immediate conflict filtering. It extracts a place from the RHS with `place` and normalizes the two places into a candidate pair with `places_to_candidate_pair`.

Collects write/read information for a terminator after clearing prior state with `reset`. It records destination writes with `add_place` and input uses with `add_operand` for calls, switch/assert discriminants, and inline-asm operands.
Records a write to a place by pushing its local into the writes list.
Records operand effects for conflict analysis. It treats `Move` as a write-like conflict source by calling `add_place`, while ignoring `Copy` and constants.
Clears per-location write-tracking state by emptying the writes list with `clear` and resetting the skipped-pair marker.

Converts two plain local places into a normalized candidate pair for merging. It rejects projected places, canonicalizes order with `swap`, and consults `is_local_required` to prefer the removable local as the source.

Builds the forward and reverse maps of possible destination-propagation merges. It clears previous storage, visits the body with `visit_body`, deduplicates candidate vectors with `sort` and `dedup`, and then populates the reverse map using `entry`, `or_default`, and `push`.

Identifies `dest = src`-style assignments that may be merged. It normalizes places with `places_to_candidate_pair`, rejects borrowed locals with `contains`, rejects non-removable sources with `is_local_required`, and records surviving candidates with `entry`, `or_default`, and `push`.
Reports whether a local must be preserved in MIR by checking its kind with `local_kind`; arguments and the return pointer are required, while temporaries are not.

Dumps MIR annotated with liveness information for debugging. It invokes `dump_mir`, lazily computes reachability with `get_or_insert_with` and `reachable_as_bitset`, and for reachable points updates the liveness cursor with `seek_after_primary_effect`, `seek_before_primary_effect`, or `seek_to_block_start` before printing.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elabora: Coordinates the ElaborateDrops MIR pass: gathers move data, calls `remove_dead_unwinds` to prune no-op drop unwinds, builds initialized/uninitialized dataflow results, constructs an `ElaborateDropsCtxt`, calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::elaborate` to generate the patch, then applies the patch and runs `deref_finder`.

Scans cleanup drop terminators and removes unwind edges for drops proven to be no-ops by maybe-initialized analysis. It builds a `MaybeInitializedPlaces` cursor, checks drop children with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, and rewrites matching unwinds to `UnwindAction::Unreachable`.
Synchronizes both initialization cursors to just before a location by calling `seek_before_primary_effect` on `inits` and `uninits`.
Returns whether a move path may be initialized and may be uninitialized by calling `contains` on both `inits` and `uninits`.
Implements a no-op debug formatter that always returns `Ok(())`.
Returns the mutable MIR patch stored in the elaboration context.
Returns the MIR body from the elaboration context.
Returns the type context from the elaboration context.
Returns the parameter environment by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::param_env`.

Classifies a drop as `Dead`, `Static`, `Conditional`, or `Open` from initialization state. In shallow mode it calls `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, calling `tcx`, `body`, and `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead` for each child.

Clears synthesized drop flags for a path. In shallow mode it calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_children_bits`, using `tcx`, `body`, `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, and `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag` on each child.
Finds the move-path child for a specific field by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific array element constant index by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the dereference child move path by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific downcast variant by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Returns the operand used to read a synthesized drop flag by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::drop_flag` and mapping the resulting place to `Operand::Copy`.
Returns the move-data environment stored in the context.
Returns the parameter environment stored in the context.
Lazily allocates a boolean local for a move path's drop flag by calling `MirPatch::new_internal` through `get_or_insert_with`.
Returns the place for an already-created drop-flag local by mapping the stored local with `Place::from`.

Performs full drop elaboration setup and flag instrumentation. It calls `collect_drop_flags`, `elaborate_drops`, `drop_flags_on_init`, `drop_flags_for_fn_rets`, `drop_flags_for_args`, and `drop_flags_for_locs`, then returns the accumulated patch.

Finds drop paths that need runtime flags by visiting reachable drop terminators, syncing analysis state with `InitializationData::seek_before`, resolving paths with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, querying liveness with `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead`, walking drop descendants with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, and calling `create_drop_flag` for children that may be both live and dead.

Rewrites reachable drop terminators into precise drop control flow. For each tracked drop it calls `InitializationData::seek_before`, resolves the move path with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, computes unwind targets using patch helpers, and invokes `rustc_mir_dataflow::elaborate_drops::elaborate_drop`; untracked non-replace drops trigger a delayed bug.
Builds a boolean MIR constant `Rvalue` for the given span and value.
Emits an assignment to a synthesized drop flag if one exists for the path. It calls `constant_bool` to build the assigned value and `MirPatch::add_assign` to insert the write.
Initializes all synthesized drop flags to `false` at function entry by calling `constant_bool` once and emitting assignments with `MirPatch::add_assign` for every stored flag.

Marks call destinations as initialized on cleanup-return edges of calls with cleanup unwinds. It resolves the destination with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, walks affected bits with `on_lookup_result_bits`, and calls `set_drop_flag` with `DropFlagState::Present`.
Applies entry-state drop-flag effects for function arguments by calling `rustc_mir_dataflow::drop_flag_effects_for_function_entry`, which in turn calls `set_drop_flag` for each affected path.

Applies non-drop location-based drop-flag updates across reachable original basic blocks. It calls `rustc_mir_dataflow::drop_flag_effects_for_location` for each statement/location, forwarding each effect to `set_drop_flag`; for certain call terminators it also resolves the destination with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, walks bits with `on_lookup_result_bits`, and calls `set_drop_flag` to mark the return place present before the critical edge.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_dataflow/src/elaborat: Returns the boolean meaning of a drop-flag state: `Present` maps to `true` and `Absent` maps to `false`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns whether this unwind mode is already in cleanup context, yielding `false` for `Unwind::To(..)` and `true` for `Unwind::InCleanup`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Converts the internal `Unwind` representation into a MIR `UnwindAction`, turning `Unwind::To(bb)` into `Cleanup(bb)` and `Unwind::InCleanup` into `Terminate`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Applies a block-mapping function to the target of `Unwind::To`, while leaving `Unwind::InCleanup` unchanged. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that returns mutable access to the `MirPatch` used to insert or rewrite MIR during drop elaboration. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that provides access to the MIR body being elaborated. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that returns the type context needed for type queries during drop elaboration. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that returns the parameter environment used when normalizing and checking whether fields need drop. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Trait hook that classifies how a path should be dropped for a given flag mode, driving whether elaboration emits dead, static, conditional, or open drop logic. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that fetches the operand representing a path's drop flag, if one exists. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that emits the update clearing a path's drop flag at a given location and mode. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that resolves the tracked subpath for a field projection, if that field has its own drop-flag path. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that resolves the tracked subpath reached through a dereference projection, if one exists. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that resolves the tracked subpath for a particular enum variant after downcasting. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Trait hook that resolves the tracked subpath for an array element subrange or index, if one exists. Trait declaration only; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Public entry point that builds a `DropCtxt` for one drop site and delegates the actual MIR expansion to `DropCtxt::elaborate_drop`.
Computes the type of a MIR place in the current body using the type context. It calls `body` and `tcx`.
Convenience accessor that forwards to the elaborator's type context. It calls `DropElaborator::tcx`.

Chooses the concrete elaboration strategy for the current drop site based on `drop_style`: dead drops become a direct goto, static drops become a direct `Drop` terminator, conditional drops branch to `complete_drop`, and open drops branch to `open_drop`. It calls `drop_style`, `patch`, `complete_drop`, `open_drop`, and `Unwind::into_action`.

Builds the `(field place, optional field subpath)` list for all fields of a variant, normalizing each field type and asking the elaborator for field subpaths. It calls `field_subpath`, `tcx`, and `param_env`.

Builds drop MIR for one child place: if a dedicated subpath exists, it creates a nested `DropCtxt` and delegates to `elaborated_drop_block`; otherwise it performs a `complete_drop` guarded by the parent path's flag. It calls `complete_drop`.
Constructs one side of a field-drop ladder by walking fields in reverse order and chaining each field drop to the next successor. It calls `drop_subpath`.
Creates the bottom of a drop ladder by clearing the shallow master drop flag before continuing to the original successor/unwind. It calls `drop_flag_reset_block`.

Builds the full field-by-field drop ladder for an aggregate after filtering out fields whose types do not need drop; when unwind edges exist, it also builds a parallel unwind half-ladder. It calls `place_ty`, `tcx`, `param_env`, and `drop_halfladder`.

Expands an open drop for a tuple by collecting each field place and subpath, creating the ladder bottom, and then building a field-drop ladder. It calls `tcx`, `field_subpath`, `drop_ladder_bottom`, and `drop_ladder`.

Finds the boxed value inside the nested `Box` representation, resolves the dereference subpath for that interior, and emits a drop for the pointee before outer box handling continues. It calls `tcx`, `deref_subpath`, and `drop_subpath`.

Expands an open drop for an ADT: empty ADTs become an unreachable block, unions and `ManuallyDrop` skip content drops, ordinary contents are handled by `open_drop_for_adt_contents`, boxes additionally drop their pointee via `open_drop_for_box_contents`, and ADTs with destructors route through `destructor_call_block`. It calls `patch`, `tcx`, `Unwind::is_cleanup`, `open_drop_for_adt_contents`, `destructor_call_block`, `Unwind::map`, and `open_drop_for_box_contents`.

Builds the content-dropping portion of an ADT open drop by first creating the ladder bottom, then using `move_paths_for_fields` plus `drop_ladder` for single-variant ADTs or delegating enums to `open_drop_for_multivariant`. It calls `drop_ladder_bottom`, `move_paths_for_fields`, `drop_ladder`, and `open_drop_for_multivariant`.

Builds variant-specific drop ladders for an enum, including separate unwind ladders when needed, and then dispatches on the discriminant to the appropriate variant drop path while handling otherwise/fallback cases. It calls `Unwind::is_cleanup`, `tcx`, `move_paths_for_fields`, `drop_halfladder`, `drop_ladder`, `param_env`, `goto_block`, `drop_block`, `adt_switch_block`, and `Unwind::map`.

Creates a block that reads the ADT discriminant into a temporary and switches to the prebuilt variant blocks, then guards that switch behind the relevant drop-flag test. It calls `tcx`, `patch`, and `drop_flag_test_block`.

Builds a MIR call block that invokes the type’s `Drop::drop` destructor on `self.place` via a mutable reference, then clears the shallow drop flag for the path at block entry and returns a guarding test block. Calls `new_temp`, `assign`, `drop_flag_test_block`, and uses `elaborator.clear_drop_flag` and `elaborator.patch().new_block`.

Constructs the basic-block loop that drops each indexed element of an array/slice range: one block computes the current element pointer and increments the index, another tests whether the loop is finished, and the drop terminator is patched to iterate or exit. Calls `new_temp`, `constant_usize`, and `assign`, and uses `elaborator.patch().new_block` plus `elaborator.patch().patch_terminator`.

Expands an open drop for arrays by analyzing which element subpaths are independently tracked; for fixed-size arrays it compresses contiguous droppable regions and preserved moved-out elements into a reverse drop ladder, otherwise it falls back to a loop-based strategy. Calls `drop_ladder_bottom`, `drop_ladder`, and `drop_loop_pair`, and uses `elaborator.array_subpath` to decide the plan.

Builds the entry/reset structure around `drop_loop` for slices or dynamically-sized array drops: creates temps for length and cursor, optionally builds an unwind-side loop, initializes the loop state, clears deep drop flags before iteration, and guards execution with a flag test. Calls `new_temp`, `drop_loop`, `constant_usize`, `assign`, `drop_flag_reset_block`, and `drop_flag_test_block`, and uses `elaborator.patch().new_block`.

Dispatches open-drop elaboration based on the place type: tuples/closure upvars/generator upvars go to tuple handling, ADTs to ADT-specific handling, trait objects to a full drop, fixed arrays to array handling, and slices to loop-based dropping. Calls `open_drop_for_tuple`, `open_drop_for_adt`, `complete_drop`, `open_drop_for_array`, and `drop_loop_pair`.
Creates a normal drop block for the whole place and then wraps it in a drop-flag test so the drop only runs when the path is considered present. Calls `drop_block` and `drop_flag_test_block`.

Creates a block that clears the path’s drop flag in the requested mode before continuing to `succ`, except on cleanup unwinds where the flag will never be read again and the successor is returned directly. Calls `new_block` and uses `elaborator.clear_drop_flag`.
Allocates a plain drop block and immediately elaborates that block in place, returning the block id for later wiring. Calls `drop_block` and `elaborate_drop`.
Builds a basic block whose terminator performs a MIR `Drop` of `self.place` to the given target with the given unwind behavior. Calls `new_block`.
Builds a basic block containing only a `Goto` terminator to the target, preserving the requested unwind cleanup classification. Calls `new_block`.

Chooses how to branch based on the path’s shallow drop style: return the unset target for dead paths, the set target for always-live paths, or emit a conditional block that tests the stored drop flag for conditional/open drops. Calls `new_block` and uses `elaborator.drop_style` plus `elaborator.get_drop_flag`.
Utility that allocates an empty MIR basic block with the supplied terminator and cleanup bit through the patcher. Uses `elaborator.patch().new_block`.
Allocates a new temporary local of the given type at the current source span through the MIR patch. Uses `elaborator.patch().new_temp`.
Constructs an `Operand::Constant` holding a `usize` literal for the current source span.
Constructs a MIR assignment statement from `lhs` to `rhs` using the current source info.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/copy_pr: Checks whether the CopyProp MIR pass should run by querying the session MIR optimization level and requiring it to be at least 1.
Entry point for the pass that logs the body definition id and then calls `propagate_ssa` to perform copy propagation on the MIR body.

Drives SSA-based copy propagation for a body: collects borrowed locals, builds SSA information, calls `fully_moved_locals` to compute which sources remain movable, derives storage markers to remove from copy classes, runs `Replacer::visit_body_preserves_cfg` to rewrite the body, and calls `crate::simplify::remove_unused_definitions` if any local was replaced.

Computes a bitset of SSA locals that are fully moved by starting from all locals as movable, scanning SSA assignments to clear locals used by copy-like reads, and then calling `ssa.meet_copy_equivalence` to merge the result across copy-equivalent locals.
Returns the typing context stored in the replacer for use by the MIR mutation visitor.
Rewrites a local to its copy-class representative for value uses, leaves storage statements unchanged, and asserts mutating uses already target the representative local.

Rewrites a place by first updating its projection with `process_projection`, rebuilding projection internals via `tcx`, and then calling `visit_local` on the base local unless the use observes the local's address directly or debuginfo requires preserving a borrowed local.
Converts propagated `Move` operands into `Copy` when the source local is not fully moved and the place has no deref, then calls `super_operand` to continue recursive operand rewriting.

Removes storage statements for eliminated representative locals, calls `super_statement` to recursively rewrite the statement, and then deletes tautological self-assignments created by propagation when both sides become the same place.
Determines whether the MIR inlining pass is enabled from session settings, honoring an explicit `inline_mir` override and otherwise checking `sess.mir_opt_level()`. Calls `mir_opt_level`.

Runs the inline pass on a body and, if inlining changed the MIR, performs cleanup and follow-up analysis. Calls `inline`, then `CfgSimplifier::new(...).simplify`, `remove_dead_blocks`, and `deref_finder`.

Top-level inlining entry point that rejects non-function/closure bodies, promoted bodies, and coroutine bodies, then constructs an `Inliner`, scans all basic blocks, and returns whether any inlining occurred. Calls `Inliner::process_blocks`.

Walks a range of caller basic blocks looking for inlineable callsites, enforces a depth-based inline budget, and recursively processes newly inlined blocks after successful splicing. Calls `resolve_callsite`, `try_inlining`, and recursively calls `process_blocks`.

Performs the main legality and compatibility checks for one callsite: verifies callee MIR availability and codegen compatibility, rejects unsized arguments, loads and validates callee MIR, checks type/signature compatibility, and finally splices the callee into the caller. Calls `check_mir_is_available`, `check_codegen_attributes`, `try_instance_mir`, `check_mir_body`, `validate_types`, `util::relate_types`, and `inline_call`.

Checks whether a callee has callable MIR and whether querying it is safe for inlining, rejecting self-recursion, MIR-less instances, and local cycle-risk cases while allowing constructors and shim-like instances.

Examines a basic block terminator and, for a direct `FnDef` call with normalized arguments and a resolvable non-virtual/non-intrinsic instance not already in the inline history, builds a `CallSite` description for later inlining.

Rejects callees whose codegen attributes make them unsafe or undesirable to inline, including `#[inline(never)]`, non-exported nongeneric cross-crate callees, C-variadic ABIs, cold functions, and incompatible sanitizer, instruction-set, or target-feature settings.

Evaluates whether the callee MIR body is profitable and structurally acceptable to inline by computing an inline threshold, traversing reachable blocks with `CostChecker`, and accounting for CFG details such as drop unwind edges and inline assembly. Calls `CostChecker::new` and `checker.visit_basic_block_data`.

Splices a callee body into the caller at a callsite: removes the original call terminator, creates a return block if needed, protects complex destinations with a temporary borrow, materializes argument locals, remaps locals/blocks/scopes through an integrator, and merges the callee MIR into the caller. Calls nested helper `dest_needs_borrow`, and also calls `new_call_temp` and `make_call_args`.
Checks whether a call destination place contains a dereference or indexing projection and therefore must be borrowed through a temporary before inlining.

Builds the caller-side locals that will serve as callee arguments, including special tuple unpacking for `RustCall` closures and temporary creation for operands that cannot be reused directly. Calls `create_temp_if_necessary`.
Reuses an argument operand if it is already a moved temporary local; otherwise allocates a new call temporary and inserts an assignment to hold the operand for inlined use. Calls `new_call_temp`.
Allocates a new temporary local for inlining, inserts `StorageLive` at the callsite, and inserts matching `StorageDead` at the return block when one exists.

Computes inlining cost for a MIR statement by ignoring `StorageLive`, `StorageDead`, `Deinit`, and `Nop`, and adding a normal instruction cost for all other statement kinds. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
